title: Ballgame: Replacing Relativistic Warping with the Mechanical Logic of Phase Symmetry
description:
This paper identifies a fundamental structural error in Einstein’s Special and General Relativity, proposing instead a model of Hardware Logic based on Phase Symmetry and Inner Coherence. The author argues that contemporary physics relies on "nonsense fillers"—such as time dilation, dark matter, and complex probability amplitudes (i)—to mask failures in initial reference frame constraints.

By utilizing a grounded thought experiment involving an extendable train platform and a "ball" (potential), the paper demonstrates that what is currently measured as "Relativity" is actually the mechanical overhead of a disconnected system maintaining coherence during an open phase. The model proves that "Time" is an Order of Sequence required to resolve asymmetry in space to create direction. When a system reaches a state of perfect symmetry (the "Singularity of Identity" or the number 1), space and time effectively cease to exist.

The paper further applies this logic to the Collatz Conjecture, GPS clock drift, and atomic stability, concluding that the universe is not a series of statistical probabilities, but a finite mechanical structure governed by the requirement of phase closure and preservation of identity.
